observations: Implementation describes source capability only, not this device health or external commissioning. Customer OAuth and optional encrypted storage are implemented; current sign-in, storage and provider readiness require separate live evidence.

components.label: Local control API
components.purpose: Loopback setup and explicitly enabled Guardian, execution and maintenance controls. Strict session/CSRF/Origin boundaries; source capability is separate from native/provider readiness.
components.diagnosticScope: Read the sanitized local setup projection; this does not prove external connectivity.

components.label: Setup and account interface
components.purpose: Setup, Connections, engine drafts, actual runtime status and System care. Installation, provider proof and draft preferences remain separate.
components.diagnosticScope: Explain the saved step and unavailable connections. Do not automate arbitrary browser tabs.

components.label: Local AI credential vault
components.purpose: Opt-in passphrase-unlocked encrypted storage for the customer Claude sign-in and assistant history. Native terminal entry only; no secret in wizard state or model context.
components.diagnosticScope: Never read or return a key, passphrase, cookie, token or secret endpoint. Snapshot cannot verify vault unlock.

components.label: Customer OpenClaw runtime
components.purpose: Isolated opt-in customer OpenClaw runtime running Claude (Opus 5.5 with Sonnet 5 fallback) with a fresh identity. The product helper has no model tools. Supports session-only state or optional encrypted storage.
components.diagnosticScope: Do not discover or reuse other agent accounts, directories, browser profiles or service configuration. Runtime installation is not unrestricted repair authority.

components.label: User-owned Claude sign-in
components.purpose: Customer connects their own Claude subscription (setup-token) or Anthropic API key in a native terminal, followed by a separate response check. No other AI provider is offered.
components.diagnosticScope: Never collect tokens or keys in chat. Do not infer API credit from a subscription or claim support without a tested supported flow.

components.label: Personal ICT assistant
components.purpose: Packaged ICT mentor agent on the customer runtime. Teaches ICT concepts from an own-words knowledge pack and reasons about chart context the user supplies. Tools: session time and public web pages only.
components.diagnosticScope: Education only. No trading, account, file, shell or broker access. Never presents output as financial advice or a signal.

components.label: Packaged strategy metadata
components.purpose: Seven named strategies and paired-engine display labels, with explicit installed/commissioning limits. Catalog presence is not an installed or ready engine.
components.diagnosticScope: Count inventory only. Catalog presence, inspected rows and saved selection do not indicate a ready bot.

components.label: Strategy access request
components.purpose: Sends the TradingView username the user typed (and an optional contact) to Decrypt Labs, which grants invite-only strategies to that username. No machine or account data is sent. If the send fails, the app shows the username to send by hand.
components.diagnosticScope: Report only the latest request status. Omit the username and contact.

components.label: TradingView customer connection
components.purpose: A customer-only TradingView web-app launcher is packaged for ARM. Actual login and script/chart/provider verification remain unqualified.
components.diagnosticScope: No provider browser access or automated login exists in this diagnostic contract.

components.label: Guardian saved logins
components.purpose: Separate opt-in encrypted local Tradovate and TradingView logins, an owned customer browser, bounded session recovery and manual handling of two-factor authentication. Restart requires vault unlock. No order actions.
components.diagnosticScope: Snapshot lists source capability only. Current sign-in and vault state must be checked in Connections; never return passwords, cookies or authentication tokens.

components.label: Tradovate native broker confirmation
components.purpose: Soup's orders go to the Tradovate bridge module's loopback /order route. Before every send the bridge must report the bound account and contract; the first entry needs a fresh flat account. Broker events come from the bridge's adapter database. Unknown quantities and uncertain sends remain unresolved.
components.diagnosticScope: Missing broker data never means flat. Do not change accounts, resend orders or infer broker acceptance/fills.

components.label: Dated market-data adapters
components.purpose: Dedicated customer browser, exact dated chart and native post-start quotes/completed bars. Stale or lost callbacks invalidate market data and require explicit reconnect.
components.diagnosticScope: Do not infer feed health from an open chart or a running process.

components.label: Durable signal delivery
components.purpose: Instance-bound secret authentication, bounded input, durable deduplication and no replay after restart. Customer-owned public HTTPS proxy/delivery acceptance remains separate.
components.diagnosticScope: Local API reachability is not public ingress proof. Do not expose admin endpoints or probe arbitrary URLs.

components.label: Contract reference calendar
components.purpose: Reviewed dated-contract and entry-only session gate through its bounded calendar horizon. Conservative holiday holds are operator policy, not a claim of full-day exchange closure; no automatic rollover.
components.diagnosticScope: Inspect source capability only. Runtime calendar entry eligibility is separate from enabled controls, bridge account state and market freshness.

components.label: Contract migration and market policy
components.purpose: Wrong/current-contract and expired-calendar entry holds are implemented. Exposure-aware contract migration and ledger reconciliation remain unimplemented; never automatically rebind a used instance.
components.diagnosticScope: Never switch ticker, rewrite historical receipts, bypass a pause or activate a new contract from calendar presence.

components.label: Customer deterministic execution lane
components.purpose: Hash-paired held Soup/FVG/Silver runtime adapters with independent ledgers, durable signals, native proof and explicit demo arming. Publication/provider commissioning remains unverified; draft-only modules are not operational protection.
components.diagnosticScope: Assistant cannot send orders, edit engine databases, change risk or enable trading. Protective execution must not depend on AI availability.

components.label: Customer desktop ownership
components.purpose: Dedicated app profiles and reviewed launcher ownership cases. Exact beta native repeated launch, graphics and cold boot require fresh acceptance.
components.diagnosticScope: Do not move arbitrary windows, restart browsers or stop services. Known-tab repair needs its own scoped implementation and tests.

components.label: Bounded maintenance and notifications
components.purpose: Bounded Guardian recovery and optional durable desktop health transitions/retry receipts. Notification acceptance is not user-read proof. No general model-driven repair or order replay.
components.diagnosticScope: Read-only scope can explain limits, not repair every issue. Escalate unknown order state; never blindly retry an order.

components.label: Customer backup and restore
components.purpose: Encrypted known-state backup, optional credential inclusion and journaled held restore. Browser cookies excluded; independent storage and native recovery acceptance remain separate.
components.diagnosticScope: Do not copy private developer backups or restore old order outboxes into active trading.

components.label: Signed installation and updates
components.purpose: Exact signed payload inventory, increasing release sequence, explicit held activation and code rollback without ledger rewind. Native update/boot/rollback acceptance remains unverified.
components.diagnosticScope: Source tests are not clean-install evidence. Do not install untrusted packages, perform disruptive updates or copy another machine's system image.
